articles.headlineJa: 第7週のファンタジー・フットボール：フレックスおよびスーパーフレックスのランキング
articles.descriptionJa: 今週、評価の近い選手の間でどちらを選ぶべきか迷っていますか？エリック・カラベルのランキングがその判断をサポートします。
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Patriots-Bears game.

-->
Teams on bye in Week 7: Bills, Chargers, Commanders, Jaguars

Week 7 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 vs GB

He scored 17.7 points in his worst game this season. Week 7 will not be his worst game. 
 2. Puka Nacua, WR1 @ LV

Only seven targets in Week 6, but expect at least double that most weeks now.
 3. Ja'Marr Chase, WR2 @ BAL

 4. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR3 vs KC

 5. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 @ SEA

He spent four seasons in Seattle. This is a revenge game. Then again, the season has been a revenge season for him.
 6. Christian McCaffrey, RB3 @ ATL

Season-high volume after Mike Evans left Monday. Be careful what you wish for, investors.
 7. Brock Purdy, QB1 @ ATL

Naysayers can point to three consecutive games with fewer than 20 points. We're not naysayers here.
 8. Jordan Love, QB2 @ DET

 9. Drake Maye, QB3 @ CHI

His season trajectory sure changed. So did the ease of schedule, but he should thrive again this week.
 10. Bijan Robinson, RB4 vs SF

How does this fellow get only 11 touches in a football game? Falcons must do better this week.
 11. Derrick Henry, RB5 vs CIN

 12. Kyren Williams, RB6 @ LV

Perhaps the loss of Davante Adams pushes Rams to run more. The current plan is not working.
 13. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR4 vs GB

No trepidation here, but he really has not lit up the Packers in recent seasons. 
 14. Justin Jefferson, WR5 vs IND

 15. CeeDee Lamb, WR6 @ PHI

 16. Brock Bowers, TE1 vs LAR

His targets have dropped each of the past three weeks. Expect that streak to end this week.
 17. Lamar Jackson, QB4 vs CIN

 18. Joe Burrow, QB5 @ BAL

 19. C.J. Stroud, QB6 vs NYG

Nobody thought he would have the fifth-most points among QBs. It looks legit, though.
 20. Jared Goff, QB7 vs GB

 21. Matthew Stafford, QB8 @ LV

Nobody is throwing more than him, but losing Adams is a really big deal. 
 22. Malik Nabers, WR7 @ HOU

He looks awesome lately, but should we forget what his new QB did to Justin Jefferson last season?
 23. Christian Watson, WR8 @ DET

 24. Matthew Golden, WR9 @ DET

 25. Caleb Williams, QB9 vs NE

He completed 83.3% of passes in Week 6. That's awesome. He also ran just four times for three yards. Hmmm.
 26. Bryce Young, QB10 vs TB

 
 27. Aaron Rodgers, QB11 @ NO

Love the matchup at New Orleans, but we must assume the Steelers don't want him throwing 49 times again.

articles.body:
The Champions!

It's another week, and that means another round of European heavyweights ready to take center stage.

The UEFA Champions League returns Tuesday for Matchday 3 of the league phase, with nine matches across the continent and plenty of mouthwatering clashes on the schedule.

Among the standout fixtures, defending champions Paris Saint-Germain welcome Barcelona in a blockbuster showdown, Liverpool host Villarreal at Anfield, and Atlético Madrid travel to Germany to face Stuttgart.

Elsewhere, Manchester City take on AEK Athens, while Napoli host Bodø/Glimt.

Also on the schedule, we have two early matches -- Fenerbahçe vs. Slavia Prague and Sabah vs. Borussia Dortmund -- before closing out the day with AS Roma vs. Slovan Bratislava and FC Porto vs. PSV Eindhoven.

Enjoy all the updates from Tuesday's matches across Europe.

articles.headline: Knockout league pickups: Trio of Lions among best pickups for Week 7
articles.description: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.
articles.headlineJa: ノックアウト・リーグの獲得候補：第7週のベストピックアップにライオンズの3選手が選出
articles.descriptionJa: トリスタン・H・コッククロフトが、敗退したチームに共通する選手をリストアップし、今週どれくらいのFAB（予算）を投入すべきかを解説します。
articles.body:
Congratulations if you survived the great Detroit Lions bye week of 2026.

Lions players occupy three of the top-12 leaderboard spots in terms of fantasy points per game (Jahmyr Gibbs No. 1, Jared Goff No. 5 and Amon Ra-St. Brown No. 12), and from a team perspective, they're second in points scored per game (32.8) and fourth in yards per game (393.8). Unsurprisingly, those three found themselves among the 16 most common players on knocked out teams in Week 6.

As discussed in this space last week, the bye weeks -- especially those that land early in the season -- present big obstacles to Knockout league success, but getting them behind is significantly advantageous. As you'll see below, Week 7's theme is going all in on players who now have full availability. This was also true with Kenneth Walker III in this space last week, and between him and Gibbs, the top two running backs in fantasy points per game now have that huge strategic schedule advantage.

It's now a (fairly) standard league

Additionally, six weeks in the books means we're down to 12 teams. Though not yet matching ESPN's standard league size, 12-team leagues aren't uncommon in fantasy football. It means richer overall rosters, compounding the bye-week problem when most Knockout leagues afford only four bench spots.

Whereas on draft day, players with late byes -- such as Derrick Henry (Week 13 bye) and CeeDee Lamb (Week 14) -- were more appealing, those individuals will become increasingly less valuable the deeper we get into the year. It's one of the reasons you'll find that recommended FAB bids are marked up for players past their byes. Solving those absence problems now, with a locked-in starter, can be advantageous.

Flexibility can be a handy thing during the byes

Speaking of those four bench spots, for managers facing injury questions -- primetime game players Rashee Rice and Saquon Barkley fall into this category for Week 7 -- keeping a space freed up for late flexibility is worth considering. That goes both for Rice's and Barkley's managers as well as any competitor who might be facing a close call for who gets knocked out after Sunday's main slates are complete.

My rule of thumb with my bench from this point forward (and accounting for the now-12 teams and soon-to-be fewer) is that if the player has no utility for me in the given week, he's a viable cut. That means my backup quarterback or WR3 type who isn't earning a start is free to go, knowing that the free agent pool is getting progressively richer and those players are easier to replace the following week.

For example, if I'm Rice's manager, I might want to clear another roster space for Dameon Pierce, Ryan Flournoy or Rashid Shaheed, if only to have a fallback ready in advance in case Rice's lineup decision goes down to kickoff time. articles.headline: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany doubtful for Arsenal game due to virus
articles.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has a viral infection which is affecting his legs and is doubtful to attend Wednesday's Champions League home game against Arsenal.
articles.body:
MUNICH -- Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has a viral infection which is affecting his legs and is doubtful to attend Wednesday's Champions League home game against Arsenal.

Assistant coach Aaron Danks said Tuesday that Kompany might need three more days to recover, as he spent the day at home.

- Champions League Power Rankings before MD3: Who's No. 1?

- Kane sets latest Bundesliga record in 100th game

"It has affected his legs at times and he's felt some pain," Danks said as he took Kompany's place at Bayern's pre-game news conference.

"It's just a virus. The doctors, the experts, know way more than I do. The most important thing we've just encouraged is that he rests, he takes the time he needs, whatever that may be, however long that may be.

"Whether that's tomorrow or whether that's two, three days' time, I don't know at this moment. Getting Vince to rest is a challenge."

Kompany was subdued and remained seated in Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

Sporting director Max Eberl said at the time that Kompany, who reportedly needed help to climb stairs, had been struggling with both the virus and a hip injury.

Asked how he would be involved if he can't attend Wednesday, Danks said Bayern had worked on remote communication last season when Kompany was suspended for the 5-4 semifinal first-leg loss to Paris Saint-Germain.

Midfielder Joshua Kimmich was away for personal reasons Tuesday and Danks said he wasn't sure if that would also affect his involvement. Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer is back in training but remains a doubt after missing Bayern's last two games with a foot issue.

articles.headline: Who to add in fantasy and the bets to make when the NBA season tips off Tuesday
articles.description: Eric Moody breaks down Tuesday's NBA action as the NBA tips off with three games, highlighting the players to add in fantasy and the bets to make.
articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Tuesday

The 2026-27 NBA season tips off Tuesday with three games featuring some of the league's biggest names.

Cade Cunningham and the Pistons get things started in Detroit after winning 60 games last season. They'll face a Boston Celtics team that now pairs a healthy Jayson Tatum with Paul George following the trade that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia.

The defending champion New York Knicks open at Madison Square Garden against a 76ers team that added LeBron James and Brown to a roster already featuring Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. Philadelphia has plenty of talent, but how quickly will everyone adjust to playing together?

The final game features a Western Conference Finals rematch, with Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs hosting Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the rival Oklahoma City Thunder.

Let's take a closer look at these matchups and identify some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering for Tuesday's slate.

Fantasy stream team -- widely available players worth adding

Isaiah Hartenstein, C, Oklahoma City Thunder (rostered in 43.4% of ESPN leagues)

Hartenstein could see additional minutes in the season opener after Chet Holmgren missed the preseason with a quad injury. Holmgren is expected to play Tuesday, but Hartenstein remains an important part of Oklahoma City's frontcourt. He averaged 9.2 PPG and 9.4 RPG last season while shooting 62.2% from the field. His rebounding and efficiency make him a solid streaming option in both points and category leagues.

Cason Wallace, PG/SG, Oklahoma City Thunder (25.6%)

Wallace signed a five-year contract extension with the Thunder and is expected to move into the starting lineup following Luguentz Dort's departure. He averaged 9.3 PPG, 3.1 RPG and 2.9 APG as a starter last season. Wallace also led the league with 150 steals and 339 deflections. Wallace should see more minutes this season, making him a strong streaming option against the Spurs on Tuesday and throughout the week, especially for managers needing steals.

Duncan Robinson, SF/SG, Detroit Pistons (6.1%)

Robinson is worth considering in deeper leagues against the Celtics, especially for managers needing 3-pointers. He averaged 12.2 points and 2.9 triples per game last season while offering limited production in other categories. He's more valuable in category leagues, but managers in deeper points formats looking for additional scoring can also consider him.

articles.headline: Wizards' AJ Dybantsa (ankle) to miss season opener
articles.description: AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick in the NBA draft, will miss the Wizards' season opener Wednesday because of an ankle injury.
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards will have to wait a little longer before seeing the regular-season debut of their No. 1 pick.

AJ Dybantsa will miss the team's Wednesday night season opener against the Milwaukee Bucks with an ankle injury, coach Brian Keefe announced Tuesday.

Dybantsa will be day-to-day with the injury he suffered in Friday's preseason finale. Keefe termed the injury a mild ankle sprain Friday.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing awkwardly on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The next chance for Dybantsa to make his debut would be Friday night at home against the Toronto Raptors before the team plays at Chicago on Saturday in the first of three straight road games.

articles.headline: Cesc Fàbregas calls suggestions he could replace Michael Carrick at Man United disrespectful
articles.description: Cesc Fabregas has dismissed suggestions he could be in line to replace Michael Carrick as disrespectful.
articles.body:
COMO, Italy -- Cesc Fàbregas has dismissed suggestions he could be in line to replace Michael Carrick as disrespectful.

Fàbregas and Carrick will go head to head on Wednesday when Como face Manchester United in the Champions League.

The former Chelsea, Arsenal and Barcelona midfielder was asked at his pre-match news conference about the possibility of taking over from Carrick, who is under pressure following a run of six games without a win.

But Fàbregas refused to answer and hit back at the line of enquiry.

"I won't answer that question because I think that's not a very nice question," Fàbregas said on Tuesday.

"I don't think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side."

United travel to Italy with just two wins all season and without a victory in any competition for more than a month.

Como, meanwhile, are fifth in the Serie A table and warmed up for United's visit with a 3-1 win over Fiorentina on Sunday.

- A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?

- Erik ten Hag: Cristiano Ronaldo 'let the team down' at Man United

- Lisandro Martínez, Marcus Rashford miss Man United training ahead of Como clash

"Manchester United is a historical club I know very, very well," said Fàbregas.

"We have so much respect for who they are, for what they do, because they have incredible players.

"I know Steve Holland very well because I worked with him for years at Chelsea and I know Michael has done really well in previous clubs as well.

"Last year he did really well bringing Manchester United back to where they belong, which is the Champions League, for the first time in many years, so it's not all bad. It's an honour to host them for the first time in our history."

articles.headline: José Mourinho on Vinícius Jr.: 'No player untouchable at Real Madrid'
articles.description: José Mourinho insisted that no player is "untouchable" at Real Madrid, as Vinícius Júnior prepares to return to the starting Xl for Wednesday's UCL match.
articles.body:
José Mourinho insisted that no player is "untouchable" at Real Madrid, as Vinícius Júnior prepares to return to the starting Xl for Wednesday's Champions League game with RB Leipzig.

Vinícius is currently serving a four-game ban in LaLiga and so is only available to play in Europe, where he made an underwhelming appearance away at Roma last week, being substituted on 58 minutes as his replacement, Endrick, inspired a 4-3 win.

Mourinho has consistently backed the Brazil international this season, despite a run of poor form which has seen him contribute just one goal for his club in all competitions, and competition for his place from Madrid's record summer signing, Yan Diomande.

"Only the badge is untouchable," Mourinho said in a news conference on Tuesday. "I don't like the concept of 'untouchable' players. What makes players untouchable isn't a captain's armband, or how long they've been at the club, or their status. What makes a player untouchable is performance."

Madrid are trailing leaders Barcelona by six points in LaLiga ahead of Sunday's Clásico at Camp Nou, but they have maximum points in the Champions League so far after two wins out of two against Inter Milan and Roma.

However Mourinho said his team couldn't be considered among the favourites to win this season's competition.

"It's very early," Mourinho said. "Right now Real Madrid don't have the objective of winning the Champions League. We have the objective of qualifying [for the knockout phase]. Then, if we get the points that allow us to qualify, then we get to our second objective, to try to avoid the playoffs, which are two games with tension, and they're games you can avoid."

Mourinho made changes to his team for Sunday's LaLiga game with Sevilla at the Bernabéu, playing Arda Güler in central midfield and giving starts to Diomande and Endrick, and was rewarded with a 4-1 win.

"As I said recently, I'm not a stubborn coach," Mourinho said. "There are coaches who have an idea, and live or die by that idea. I'm not that kind of coach, I'm always open to analyse, to understand things and look for the best for the team."

Defender Ibrahima Konaté said Mourinho has "an aura that not many managers have."

"He doesn't need to speak, and everyone will listen and respect him," Konaté said. "He's a great manager, and everyone here at this club wants success with him."

Konaté was also asked about an incident in September in which he, Kylian Mbappé and Vinicius refused to wear a pre-match T-shirt supporting the Spanish city of Ceuta, in the midst of a migration crisis.

"To be honest, I didn't really understand what was on the shirt," Konaté said on Tuesday. "You have to understand, I'm from France, but my parents came from Africa. Many things happen, and many people are in the same situation as me... In that situation, I didn't understand what it meant on the shirt, and I was focused on the game."
